Optimism of the whole modelling strategy, not just of the coefficients

Source: R/full_process.R
mm_full_process.Rd

Refits the entire strategy inside every bootstrap resample and scores each refit on the development rows, so the optimism being corrected includes every data-dependent choice the strategy makes.

Usage

mm_full_process(model, cohort, B = 200L, min_valid = ceiling(0.8 * B))

Arguments

model

A mm_model().

cohort

The cohort.

B

Resamples.

min_valid

Fewest successful resamples for the result to be reported as adequate.

Value

A list with the optimism, the corrected metrics and the count of valid resamples.

Details

This is the distinction the specification insists on. rms::validate() refits one fixed formula, which corrects the optimism of estimating coefficients. It does not re-derive anything the formula was chosen or shaped by. Here the resample gets its own spline knot placement, its own datadist, and its own factor-level handling, because all three are learned from data and all three are part of what would be redone on a new sample.

What this does not yet re-execute, because the package does not do them yet, is imputation, feature selection, tuning and interaction screening. A strategy including any of those is not fully validated by this function either, and covers names what was actually repeated so the claim stays honest as the pipeline grows.

Resamples that cannot be fitted are counted rather than dropped quietly. A resample missing a factor level, or separating, is a real feature of small cohorts, and an optimism averaged over the survivors of a selection nobody reported is not the quantity it claims to be.
